questions.stem:
SCIENCE PASSAGE 3: Layered Thermal Insulation
A team wrapped identical warm-water containers with 0, 1, 2, or 3 felt layers. Experiment 1 measured water temperature after 30 minutes in still air. Experiment 2 repeated the test with a fan producing constant airflow. Every container began at 70°C and contained the same water volume.

Which follow-up would most directly strengthen or extend the investigation?

options.A: Repeat only the result that best matches the original expectation and discard the others.
options.B: Change every variable at once so that no control condition remains.
options.C: Stop collecting measurements and infer the answer from the graph title.
options.D: Measure temperature at several times to compare cooling rates rather than only final temperatures.

questions.explanation: The proposed follow-up changes or replicates conditions in a way that produces interpretable additional evidence.

questions.stem:
SCIENCE PASSAGE 7: Pendulum Period, Length, and Mass
Students timed 10 swings of pendulums with two bob masses at several string lengths and divided by 10 to obtain period. The release angle was kept small and constant.

Which conclusion is best supported by the data?

options.A: Every value in both series was identical.
options.B: Period increased with string length and was nearly unchanged when bob mass doubled.
options.C: The measured outcome changed randomly with no visible pattern.
options.D: The results prove the same pattern must occur under all untested conditions.

questions.explanation: The conclusion accurately summarizes the plotted pattern without extending beyond the tested conditions.

questions.stem:
SCIENCE PASSAGE 7: Pendulum Period, Length, and Mass
Students timed 10 swings of pendulums with two bob masses at several string lengths and divided by 10 to obtain period. The release angle was kept small and constant.

Which prediction is most consistent with the pattern and appropriately qualified?

options.F: All future measurements must equal the last measured value exactly.
options.G: Changing the x-variable cannot affect the measured outcome.
options.H: A pendulum longer than 100 cm would likely have a period greater than about 2.0 seconds.
options.J: A single plotted point proves a universal scientific law.

questions.explanation: The prediction extends the observed pattern cautiously rather than claiming certainty.

questions.stem:
SCIENCE MATERIAL SET 6
Students tested how water temperature affected the time required for a tablet to dissolve. They used identical tablets, 105 mL of water in each cup, and stirred each cup at the same rate.

TABLE 1
Temperature (°C) | Dissolving time (s)
10 | 29
20 | 21
30 | 16
40 | 12

Trial 2 repeated the procedure with twice the water volume. Researcher 1 claims that higher temperature increases particle motion and therefore decreases dissolving time. Researcher 2 agrees that temperature matters but claims that stirring rate is the dominant factor whenever stirring is not controlled.

Which conclusion goes beyond the data?

options.A: The tested tablet dissolved faster at 40°C than at 10°C.
options.B: Every substance dissolves faster at higher temperature.
options.C: Dissolving time decreased across the tested range.
options.D: The 20°C time exceeded the 40°C time.

questions.explanation: The keyed response follows the material and directly targets 判断结论是否超出数据支持范围.
